402284.title: Li Chen: A New Eastern Spirit—Genuine and Otherworldly
402284.overview:
Gana Art and Asia Art Center present the first solo exhibition in Korea of Taiwanese sculptor Li Chen (b. 1963). Working in heavy materials such as bronze, he creates rounded forms that seem to float, in a language that neither stays within tradition nor copies Western models. He has shown at a collateral event of the 52nd Venice Biennale, and his work is in major public collections worldwide.

The show surveys work from 1999 to 2025, from Energy of Emptiness and Spiritual Journey through the Great Ether to the recent Celestial Manuscripts. His swelling bronze forms feel filled with air or energy, reflecting his idea of a 'New Eastern Spirit' that carries classical thought into contemporary form.

402285.title: Inside Paradise
402285.overview:
Ira Choi's 'paradises' and 'oases' are less utopias than worlds built from memory and imagination. This exhibition steps inside them: deserts and forests, seas and highlands, moonlight and golden trees, inhabited by leopards, pandas, flamingos, birds, butterflies and a small traveller. The leopard, painted with heart-shaped eyes and nose, acts as the paradise's guardian.

The landscapes grow from the artist's childhood memories of a 'secret garden' her father made. She builds up oil paint with metal knives she forges herself, creating a thick, layered texture.

402907.title: Mun Jun-ho: Landscapes for What Remains
402907.overview:
A solo show by Mun Jun-ho, who paints with silicone sealant, a material emblematic of modern industry, to depict the vastness of nature and the finitude of human civilisation. His realistic yet reimagined utopian landscapes of forests, light, waterfalls and rivers, often scattered with ruins, play on stark black-and-white contrast and a thick, rubbery texture. Large paintings are shown alongside small silicone drawings of factories and military life.

Open 20 October to 13 November 2026; closed Sundays and public holidays. Weekdays 10:00–18:00, Saturdays 11:00–17:00. Booking a day ahead is recommended.

402977.title: The Unfamiliar Within the Familiar
402977.overview:
We look at a familiar world every day, but does familiarity mean we truly know it? The same object looks different depending on time, memory and experience, and the familiar can turn strange at any moment, often because our way of seeing has changed rather than the thing itself.

This exhibition explores that subtle gap. Objects and landscapes on the canvas are more than representations: light and colour blur boundaries and evoke traces of time and feeling. The strangeness arises not from a new world but from inside the one we know too well. Curated by Kwon Do-eun.

405230.title: Amid Countless Beginnings
405230.overview: A two-person show by Kim Da-um and Im Sang-bin, running 24 October to 17 November. Working in different visual languages, both explore the change and possibility that arise between chance and rule, the one and the many. Kim arranges the unpredictable flows and drying marks of paint into repeated forms and patterns, reflecting an uncertain future and the routines of daily life. Im traces how a single stroke connects with others and expands into new forms and worlds.

405231.title: Beloved
405231.overview:
"Who is your beloved?" In this solo show Lee Na-jin asks how beloved beings are remembered. Her young animals, wearing ornate crowns and jewels, gaze out at the viewer; the contrast of innocent eyes and heavy gold evokes both the weight of growing up and memories of childhood.

The work grew from her experience of the Great East Japan Earthquake and the death of her mentor; the crowns recall her childhood in Britain. Since 2003 she has developed a 'squeezing technique', piping paint like cake icing and building up embroidery-like layers whose colour shifts with the light.

405232.title: Ban Min-su: Who Will Go Before Us
405232.overview:
Humanity has always needed something to lead the way: gods and heroes, nations and ideologies, science and technology, and today capital and images. When we cannot tell what is right, we follow what others have chosen, and what many people look at becomes the standard.

In Ban Min-su's 'Art Auction' series, the auction house is where such belief is formed. The crowd gazes at a single work, but what they see is the value and desire attached to it. Perhaps every era has made its own new 'gods'. The exhibition follows the crowd's gaze and asks: who will go before us, and what will we believe as we follow?

405785.title: Yuichi Hirako: POSTFOREST
405785.overview:
Gallery Baton presents POSTFOREST, the third solo exhibition there by Yuichi Hirako (b. 1982), from 22 October to 5 December 2026 in Hannam-dong. Raised amid the nature of Okayama, Japan, Hirako noticed while studying in London that urban greenery exists mainly for human comfort, a concern that runs through his paintings and sculptures of hybrid, tree-like figures living alongside animals in a distant forest.

New paintings and sculptures reimagine the forest as a layered place of story, community and anonymity. For the first time he shows suspended sculptures, letting visitors walk among floating forms as if moving through a forest.

407028.title: Choi Su-ryeon: Mustard Seed Garden Grave
407028.overview:
A solo exhibition by Choi Su-ryeon, running 10 October to 7 December 2026. For several years the artist has been hand-copying Qing-dynasty tales of the strange and classical East Asian painting treatises, checking them against Korean translations. Her study notes, with Chinese characters in black, readings and translations added in whatever colours were to hand, corrections and highlighter marks, became the basis for paintings.

She imagines that one of the little mounds in the garden of the Mustard Seed Garden Manual of Painting might be a grave hiding something wicked. The show is split across two venues: large paintings modelled on Persian miniatures at Gallery Chosun, and experimental drawings at WWNN.
